fact: The flag of Nepal is a double pennon — the only non-rectangular national flag, and the only one taller than it is wide.

prompt: Citizens of which country may live and work in the UK without a visa?
fact: The Common Travel Area lets British and Irish citizens move, live and work freely between the two states.

prompt: Which country is completely surrounded by South Africa?
fact: Lesotho is the largest of only three sovereign states entirely enclosed by another country.

prompt: Which country has the only national flag with a different design on each side?
fact: Paraguay's flag is the only national flag worldwide with a unique design on each side.

prompt: Which country's parliament, founded in 930, is the oldest in the world?
fact: Iceland's Althing was established in 930 and is the oldest legislature in the world.

prompt: Which country contains the world's largest salt flat?
fact: Salar de Uyuni in Bolivia covers about 10,582 square kilometres — the largest salt flat on Earth.

prompt: Which country is home to the world's tallest waterfall?
fact: Angel Falls in Venezuela drops 979 metres — the tallest uninterrupted waterfall in the world.

prompt: Which country measures its progress using Gross National Happiness?
fact: Gross National Happiness is the guiding philosophy of the government of Bhutan.

prompt: Which country was the first in the world where all women could vote?
fact: New Zealand granted all women the vote in 1893, after a campaign led by Kate Sheppard.

prompt: Which country elected the world's first female prime minister, in 1960?
fact: Sirimavo Bandaranaike of Ceylon (now Sri Lanka) was the first woman in the world elected prime minister.

prompt: Which country's national flag is square rather than rectangular?
fact: Switzerland and Vatican City are the only states whose national flags are square.

prompt: Which country's flag shows a map of the island it occupies?
fact: The flag of Cyprus shows the island in copper-orange, for the copper ore it was probably named after.

prompt: Which country is doubly landlocked — every one of its neighbours is landlocked too?
fact: Only two countries are doubly landlocked — Uzbekistan and Liechtenstein. Reaching the sea from either means crossing at least two borders.

prompt: Which is one of the five permanent members of the UN Security Council?
fact: The five permanent members — Russia, China, the United States, the United Kingdom and France — each hold a veto. (As of 2026.)

prompt: Which is one of the five Nordic countries?
fact: The Nordic countries are Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden.

prompt: Which is one of the seven G7 countries?
fact: The G7 is Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States. (As of 2026.)

prompt: Which is one of the three Benelux countries?
fact: Benelux is a portmanteau of its three members — Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg — whose 1944 customs union became the model for the European Union.

prompt: Which is one of the ten countries the Danube flows through?
fact: The Danube passes through or borders ten countries — more than any other river on Earth — from Germany's Black Forest to the Black Sea.

prompt: Which is one of the six countries that border the Black Sea?
fact: The Black Sea is bordered by Bulgaria, Georgia, Romania, Russia, Turkey and Ukraine, and drains a basin covering almost a third of Europe.

prompt: Which is one of the three Baltic states?
fact: The Baltic states are Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. Estonian is a Finnic language, unrelated to Latvian and Lithuanian.

prompt: Which is one of the eleven OPEC member countries?
fact: OPEC has eleven members — six in Africa, four in the Middle East and one, Venezuela, in South America. Angola announced its departure in December 2023. (As of 2026.)

prompt: Which is one of the five countries that border the Caspian Sea?
fact: The Caspian is the largest inland body of water on Earth; its coastlines are shared by Azerbaijan, Iran, Kazakhstan, Russia and Turkmenistan.

prompt: Which is one of the three countries with territory on the island of Borneo?
fact: Borneo is split three ways: Indonesia holds about 73%, Malaysia 26%, and Brunei the remaining 1%.

prompt: Which is one of the two countries on the island of Hispaniola?
fact: Hispaniola is divided between Spanish-speaking Dominican Republic to the east and French- and Creole-speaking Haiti to the west.

prompt: Which is one of the four countries in the Visegrád Group?
fact: The Visegrád Group — Czechia, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia — is named after the Hungarian castle town where its leaders first met in 1991.

prompt: Which is one of the six African members of OPEC?
fact: Africa supplies six of OPEC's eleven members: Algeria, the Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Libya and Nigeria. (As of 2026.)

prompt: Which is one of the four Middle Eastern members of OPEC?
fact: OPEC's four Middle Eastern members — Iran, Iraq, Kuwait and Saudi Arabia — sit on the bulk of the cartel's proven reserves. (As of 2026.)

prompt: Which is the only South American member of OPEC?
fact: Venezuela is OPEC's sole South American member and one of its five founders — it called the 1949 meeting that set the cartel in motion.

prompt: Which is one of the five countries that founded OPEC in 1960?
fact: OPEC was founded on 14 September 1960 in Baghdad by Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela. Admitting a new member still needs the consent of all five.

prompt: Which is one of the five countries that have left OPEC?
fact: Five countries have left OPEC: Angola, Ecuador, Indonesia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. (As of 2026.)

prompt: Which is the only G7 country in Asia?
fact: Japan is the only Asian member of the G7, which it joined at the group's second summit in 1976.

prompt: Which is one of the four European members of the G7?
fact: Four of the seven are European — France, Germany, Italy and the United Kingdom — alongside Canada, Japan and the United States.

prompt: Which is one of the three Scandinavian countries?
fact: Scandinavia most commonly means Denmark, Norway and Sweden. Iceland and Finland are Nordic but not Scandinavian.

prompt: Which is the only Benelux country that is a grand duchy?
fact: Luxembourg is officially the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg — the world's only remaining sovereign grand duchy.

prompt: Which is one of the four countries whose capital city stands on the Danube?
fact: The Danube passes four national capitals — Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade — more than any other river.

prompt: Which is the only country that borders both the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea?
fact: Russia alone touches both: the Black Sea coast around Sochi, and the Caspian shore at the mouth of the Volga.

prompt: Which is the only country on the Caspian Sea that was never part of the Soviet Union?
fact: Iran holds the Caspian's southern shore; the other four coasts — Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Russia and Turkmenistan — were all Soviet republics.

prompt: Which is the only sovereign country lying entirely on the island of Borneo?
fact: Brunei occupies about 1% of Borneo and lies wholly on it; Indonesia and Malaysia, which hold the other 99%, both extend well beyond the island.

prompt: Which country occupies the western part of the island of Hispaniola?
fact: Haiti holds the western third of Hispaniola and speaks French and Haitian Creole; the Spanish-speaking Dominican Republic has the larger eastern portion.

prompt: Which is the only Visegrád Group country with a sea coast?
fact: Poland reaches the Baltic; the other three Visegrád countries — Czechia, Hungary and Slovakia — are all landlocked.

prompt: Which Baltic state speaks a Finnic language rather than a Baltic one?
fact: Estonian is a Finnic language, close to Finnish. Latvian and Lithuanian are Baltic languages, and neither is intelligible to an Estonian speaker.
